requirements.name: University of Science and Technology of China

academic.grading_system_summary: Numeric 0-100 marks; letter grades; and two-level scores (Pass/Fail) are used.
academic.academic_summary_notes: Usual workload is 15-20 credits/semester for undergraduates and 10 credits/semester for graduate students. Recommended language levels: HSK 5 for Chinese-taught courses or TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.0 for English-taught courses; recommended GPA 2.5/4.0. Exchange students do not pay tuition to USTC.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: On-campus housing is offered on a first-come, first-served basis; if full, nearby hotels or hostels may be used. Students are advised to bring approximately CNY 1000 in cash for taxi to campus and dormitory deposit.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: Exchange students must purchase Chinese medical insurance. Insurance fee: 400 CNY for six months or 800 CNY for one year. Foreign-based insurance may have slower compensation; Chinese system often requires payment before treatment.
housing_and_logistics.estimated_housing_cost_per_month: Approximately 500-1500 CNY/month per person (on-campus, varies by room type).
housing_and_logistics.estimated_living_cost_per_month: Food: approximately 60 CNY/day (~1800 CNY/month). Housing: approximately 500-1500 CNY/month. (Costs vary by lifestyle and room type.)
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Visa types: X2 for one-semester (<=180 days) and X1 for one year or longer (X1 holders must apply for a residence permit within 30 days of entry). Chinese medical insurance is mandatory and costs 400 CNY (6 months) or 800 CNY (1 year).

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: The factsheet does not specify buddy programs or mandatory orientation events. Students should follow the online application portal and the provided pre-arrival suggestions (bring cash, obtain Chinese medical insurance).

analysis.general_fit_reasoning: Top-tier ARWU research university (high STEM output) with excellent nature access (Vancouver outdoors) which supports a quieter research lifestyle, but its sprawling/commuter aspects and active city nightlife mean it's not the most secluded campus.

academic.academic_summary_notes: Exchange students register for courses on POVIS on a first-come-first-serve basis. Undergraduate recommended/standard load is 15 credits (min 10, max 22); graduate students have separate limits (min 3, max 18); nomination, CGPA >3.0/4.3 and English proficiency required.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: All international students are guaranteed a room in POSTECH student dormitory unless they choose otherwise. Housing fee must be paid in full by cash deposit to POSTECH Housing Services within the first week of the semester; a negative tuberculosis check-up in English is required to check in.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: All international students are automatically registered to the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) from the date of alien registration (approx. 70,000 KRW/month invoiced). Students must also purchase a separate insurance plan covering most illnesses and injuries valid for at least 1 month from arrival. A negative tuberculosis check-up report in English is required for dormitory check-in.
housing_and_logistics.estimated_living_cost_per_month: Approx. 715 USD/month total (Housing $125, Dining $350, Health Insurance $55, Transportation $35, Personal $150); NHIS approx. 70,000 KRW/month invoiced.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Students receive a Certificate of Admission (required for visa) and must have passport validity six months beyond program end. POSTECH is IEQAS-certified enabling a simplified visa process, ISSS assists with ARC during orientation; students must leave Korea within 30 days after program end or by ARC expiry.

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: Pre-arrival orientation is delivered by Zoom covering visa process, life at POSTECH, and course registration; on-campus Orientation for New International Students includes mandatory sessions and cultural activities, and ISSS provides guidance for alien registration and settling in.

analysis.general_fit_reasoning: Strong ARWU research university with intense STEM focus and a campus culture described as research-heavy/low-social — very compatible with 'quiet campus, research focus'; city location (Hefei) is functional rather than a major cultural hub.

academic.instruction_languages: English (some courses may be offered in Korean)
academic.academic_summary_notes: Undergraduate exchange students: minimum 4 courses (12 credits) and maximum 8 courses (24 credits). Graduate exchange students: minimum 3 courses (9 credits) and maximum 4 courses (12 credits). Course lists are uploaded ~2 months prior and course registration opens 1-2 months before the semester; students must register for courses at their appropriate degree level.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: KAIST will apply for on-campus accommodation for all exchange students based on their application form. Assigned dormitories are double or triple occupancy, furnished (bed, closet, desk, chair); shared restrooms, showers, washing machines, dryers and a lobby on each floor. KAIST provides one pillow and one blanket. Dormitory info available at KAIST Dormitory/KDS site.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: D-2 visa holders must subscribe to National Health Insurance (NHI); subscribing takes more than a month so students should prepare traveler's insurance to cover at least the first month in Korea.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Students need the KAIST Certificate of Admission to apply for a Korean student visa; KAIST ISSS provides further guidance on visa, alien registration and dormitory. D-2 visa holders must enroll in NHI and should have short-term travel insurance for the first month.

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: KAIST sends welcome packages (including Certificate of Admission and information) and the ISSS team provides further details on arrival, housing and registration. Further orientation details are provided to accepted students once procedures are finalized.

academic.academic_summary_notes: Undergraduates must take at least 9 credits per semester; graduate inbound students must take at least 2 courses. housing_and_logistics.housing_details: The Division of Overseas Student Affairs handles accommodation and host-family arrangements for international students; no explicit guarantee or deadlines stated in the factsheet.

Nomination from home institution and online application are required; admission letters are sent to home coordinators.

student_integration.language_course_details: Free Chinese courses provided by the Chinese Language Division/Language Teaching and Research Center, including Chinese Cultural Salon (cultural experience), courses from introductory to advanced (4 levels), and elective situational conversation courses; offered at no cost.
student_integration.integration_summary_notes: The Division supports international student society activities and host-family arrangements and offers free Chinese language and cultural courses to facilitate cultural and academic integration.

analysis.general_fit_reasoning: Applied-sciences focus with negligible ARWU presence (low global research footprint) but situated in a small-town/residential setting that is typically quiet and student-centered — good match for a tranquil research environment if heavy research prestige is not required.

academic.academic_summary_notes: Undergraduate exchange students are required to take a minimum of 9 credits per semester; graduate exchange students must take at least one master-level course. housing_and_logistics.housing_details: Dormitory fees administered by Division of Student Housing. housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: Exchange students staying longer than 180 days are covered by/should enroll in Taiwan National Health Insurance (NHI); links to ARC and NHI information are provided. No specific cost details provided in factsheet.
housing_and_logistics.estimated_housing_cost_per_month: Undergraduates: NT$6,300–16,660 per semester; Graduates: NT$10,170–27,500 per semester.
housing_and_logistics.estimated_living_cost_per_month: Estimated for one semester: USD 3,600 (includes dorm, visa, textbooks, food, transportation, etc.).
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Visa guidance and links are provided (Visitor/Resident Visa, ARC), but the university does not explicitly state visa sponsorship. National Health Insurance applies for exchange students staying over 180 days.

student_integration.language_course_details: Mandarin courses are available to take during the exchange. English course information is published seasonally (English course info for fall released late May; for spring released mid-December); no costs specified.
student_integration.integration_summary_notes: Office of Global Affairs and the Division of Overseas Students Service handle incoming student support; language courses and student housing options are available but specific buddy/orientation programs are not detailed in the factsheet.

KAIST provides one pillow and one blanket. Dormitory info available at KAIST Dormitory/KDS site.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: D-2 visa holders must subscribe to National Health Insurance (NHI); subscribing takes more than a month so students should prepare traveler's insurance to cover at least the first month in Korea.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Students need the KAIST Certificate of Admission to apply for a Korean student visa; KAIST ISSS provides further guidance on visa, alien registration and dormitory. D-2 visa holders must enroll in NHI and should have short-term travel insurance for the first month.

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: KAIST sends welcome packages (including Certificate of Admission and information) and the ISSS team provides further details on arrival, housing and registration. Further orientation details are provided to accepted students once procedures are finalized.
